additional_requirements: The binge eating occurs, on average, at least once a week for 3 months

S049.name: Eating_Large_Amount
S049.description: Eating, in a discrete period of time, an amount of food that is definitely larger than what most individuals would eat in a similar period of time under similar circumstances.
examples: Eating more than 3-4 times the amount of a typical meal within 2 hours.
Continuously eating large amounts of high-calorie snacks in addition to main meals.
Eating enough to empty a significant portion of the refrigerator or pantry at once.
Eating clearly more food than others during the same period of time.

S050.name: Loss_of_Control
S050.description: A sense of lack of control over eating during the episode (e.g., a feeling that one cannot stop eating or control what or how much one is eating).
examples: A feeling that once I start eating, I cannot stop even if I want to.
Thinking 'I shouldn't eat any more' but mechanically continuing to eat.
A feeling of helplessness that I cannot decide for myself how much to eat.
Eating as if my body is being controlled by someone else.

S051.name: Rapid_Eating
S051.description: Eating much more rapidly than normal.
examples: Swallowing food without chewing it properly.
Eating continuously and rapidly to the point where it is difficult to breathe.
Eating so urgently that there is no time to taste the food.
Eating at a speed that surprises others.

S052.name: Eating_Until_Uncomfortably_Full
examples: Eating until the stomach feels distended to the point of bursting and pain.
Eating so much that it is difficult to even stand up or move.
Continuing to eat until feeling nauseous or like vomiting.
Unable to stop eating even though it is physically uncomfortable and painful.

S053.name: Eating_Without_Hunger
S053.description: Eating large amounts of food when not feeling physically hungry.
examples: Starting to eat a large amount of food again immediately after finishing a meal.
A binge eating episode starting when not hungry at all.
Continuing to eat large amounts despite being full.
Seeking out food even when there are absolutely no physical hunger signals.

S054.name: Eating_Alone_Due_to_Embarrassment
S054.description: Eating alone because of feeling embarrassed by how much one is eating.
examples: Eating only when alone because of fear that others will think strangely of the amount eaten.
Eating secretly after family members have gone to sleep.
Pretending to eat little in front of people, then binging when alone.
Locking the door or eating in a secret place like a car to avoid being seen eating.

symptom.disease_info: Binge-Eating Disorder is characterized by recurrent episodes of consuming unusually large amounts of food within a discrete period, accompanied by a sense of loss of control and marked distress, but without regular compensatory behaviors such as vomiting or excessive exercise. Episodes are often associated with eating rapidly, eating when not physically hungry, eating until uncomfortably full, and subsequent shame or guilt, leading many patients to eat in secret. The disorder commonly emerges in late adolescence or young adulthood and can be chronic or recurrent, frequently linked to mood and anxiety symptoms, body-image concerns, and difficulties with emotion regulation. It is distinguished from Bulimia Nervosa primarily by the absence of purging and from normative overeating by the frequency, loss of control, and psychological distress surrounding the episodes.

patient.personality: Yamilet is an imaginative, introspective, and empathic young woman whose love of art, culture, and community is tempered by anxious perfectionism and a tendency to procrastinate and scramble near deadlines.
patient.stressor: Yamilet moved away from home for her first year of university, leaving behind the familiar structure of her family’s routines, shared meals, and cultural festivals in favor of a dorm environment with irregular schedules and buffet-style dining. Feeling both excited and overwhelmed, she coped with homesickness, social anxiety in a new city, and pressure to prove herself in a competitive museum studies program by throwing herself into late-night studio sessions and last-minute paper-writing. During these rushed stretches, she began grabbing large amounts of easily available cafeteria and takeout food between classes and before critiques, eating quickly so she could get back to painting or revising, and finding that these hurried meals temporarily soothed her nerves. Over the next ten months, this pattern solidified around exam periods and project deadlines, and she ultimately sought psychiatric care when she realized that her relationship with food during stressful academic moments felt increasingly out of control and at odds with the mindful, wellness-focused lifestyle she was trying to cultivate through yoga and meditation.
patient.chief_complaint: When I’m stressed with schoolwork, I find myself eating way faster than normal and I can’t seem to slow down.

S049.name: Eating_Large_Amount
S049.description: Eating, in a discrete period of time, an amount of food that is definitely larger than what most individuals would eat in a similar period of time under similar circumstances.
S049.manifestation: On my really bad study nights, I’ll load up two or three full plates from the dorm buffet or order a huge takeout spread just for myself and keep picking at it until there’s as much food gone as if I’d been eating with a small group of friends instead of alone in my room.

S050.name: Loss_of_Control
S050.description: A sense of lack of control over eating during the episode (e.g., a feeling that one cannot stop eating or control what or how much one is eating).
S050.manifestation: Once I start, it feels like something flips and I’m just shoveling food in even while I’m thinking, ‘You don’t need this, you should stop,’ but my hands keep moving like I’m on autopilot.

S051.name: Rapid_Eating
S051.description: Eating much more rapidly than normal.
S051.manifestation: During crunch time before critiques, I eat so fast between brushstrokes or paragraphs that I barely chew or taste anything, just swallowing quickly so I can hurry back to my canvas or my laptop.

S052.name: Eating_Until_Uncomfortably_Full
S052.manifestation: I’ll keep going past the point where my stomach feels tight and stretched and I have to lean back in my desk chair because it physically hurts, but I still nibble on whatever’s left in front of me.

S053.name: Eating_Without_Hunger
S053.description: Eating large amounts of food when not feeling physically hungry.
S053.manifestation: A lot of the time I’m not even hungry—like I’ll finish a regular dinner at the dining hall and then, as soon as I sit down to work on a paper, I get up again to grab snacks or extra food just because I feel anxious, not because my body needs it.

S054.name: Eating_Alone_Due_to_Embarrassment
S054.description: Eating alone because of feeling embarrassed by how much one is eating.
S054.manifestation: I’ve gotten into this habit of pretending I eat light salads with my friends, then later sneaking back to my dorm with a bunch of food from the late-night café so I can binge alone without anyone seeing how much I actually eat.
